## Entry state

- **Tracker.** Initialized earlier with three stages: `gather, provision, verify`. There is no `sync` stage because `--rebase` was not passed. `review`, `report` and `menu` were added as each started. Each loop re-entry below re-opens the stage it re-enters.
- **Run record.** The tracker's first task carries `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`. Before any work I validate the record:
  - It exists and is well-formed.
  - `consent.target` matches `acme/widgets`, PR `42` and base `main`.
- **Course.** The human picked `deliver with nits` numerically at the initial menu. I persisted `course: deliver-nits` with caps 10/10 and usage 0/0 before any course write.
- **Starting state.** The source head 1111111 already meets every merge prerequisite. Readiness under deliver-nits still needs a `resolved` closure line for every opted-in nit, and N1 and N2 have none. So the fixed D3 body runs with no menu.

## D3 iteration 1 (head 1111111)

1. **Exit check.**
   - There is no prior helper result and no no-progress checkpoint.
   - Readiness fails on the open nits N1 and N2.
   - No obstacle applies, and usage is 0/10 rounds and 0/10 syncs.
2. **Next-action boundary refresh (read-only).**
   - `gh pr view 42 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,...` returns head 1111111, OPEN, MERGEABLE, CLEAN, the body unchanged and base `main`, which matches the target.
   - `gh run list -R acme/widgets -c 1111111... --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url` returns run 910 with success.
3. **Fix wave setup.**
   - Record `repair.wave.pre_wave_head = 1111111`.
   - Create the per-pass checkpoint with `round_start_head 1111111`, `counted false` and `stage apply`.
   - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 fetch origin main`.
   - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0, so no sync is needed.
4. **Implementer for N1.**
   - Dispatch: `subagent({ agent: "implementer", context: "fresh", async: false, cwd: "/work/widgets-pr-42" })`.
   - The task carries the N1 evidence pack (unused import at src/guard.mjs:1). It says to apply the payload and not re-solve the finding, using the smallest in-repo edit with no new dependency or module.
   - It passes `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS = node --test src/guard.test.mjs`.
   - It passes the stored scope baseline, with the rule to return `open - contract exception: <why>` rather than change the contract.
   - Commit rule: one commit on feature/guard only when the scoped test passes. Otherwise discard its edits and return `open - <why>`.
   - Report shape: the scoped test run before and after the edit.
   - The helper returns `done`. `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 status --porcelain` is empty and `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 rev-parse HEAD` shows exactly one new commit.
5. **Implementer for N2.** I dispatch a second fresh `implementer` with the same rules and the N2 pack (duplicate guard at src/guard.mjs:6). It also returns `done`, with one new commit and a clean tree.
6. **Round accounting.** At least one source-changing commit landed, so the round counts once. I persist `counted true`, `counted_head` and `rounds_used 1`, and move to `stage review`.
7. **Loop sync.** The PR is not CONFLICTING or BEHIND and has no merge-tree conflict, so this is skipped.
8. **Pre-push review.**
   - `merge-tree` is re-run and exits 0.
   - Output path: `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-review.XXXXXX"`.
   - Dispatch: `subagent({ agent: "wave-reviewer", context: "fresh", async: false, cwd: "/work/widgets-pr-42" })`, read-only, over `1111111..HEAD`.
   - N1 and N2 are listed under `## Previous review report (re-review trigger)`, and `git diff 1111111 HEAD` is under `## Fix delta`.
   - The task asks for the native report plus one closure line per finding.
   - It returns `N1: resolved` and `N2: resolved` with no new findings, so the carried set is empty.
9. **Push.**
   - The done-check passes on the helper commit subjects.
   - Compare-and-swap: `gh pr view 42 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName` still shows 1111111, OPEN, the body unchanged and `main`.
   - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 push --no-follow-tags git@git.example.invalid:acme/widgets.git HEAD:refs/heads/feature/guard` succeeds.
   - I persist `repair.wave.pushed_head` and `headRefOid = 2222222`. `poll_deadline` stays null because no window existed to renew.
10. **Step 4 (watch).** The Exit check on the last helper result passes. Exact-head CI on 2222222 is a success with no binding pending check and no reviewer run pending, so the watch call is skipped.
11. **Own-push re-render (review stage).**
    - Pre-menu refresh: `gh pr view ...` and `gh run list -R acme/widgets -c 2222222...` show CI success, CLEAN and MERGEABLE. The comment fetches follow:
      - `gh api repos/acme/widgets/pulls/42/comments --paginate`
      - `gh api repos/acme/widgets/issues/42/comments --paginate`
      - the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query
    - No reviewer workflow is known, so there is no reviewer `gh run list`.
    - A fresh comment-delta `wave-reviewer` is dispatched with cwd `/work/widgets-pr-42`. It is read-only, uses Section C plus the baseline, and must check `rev-parse HEAD == 2222222`.
    - It reviews the delta against source at 2222222 and finds N3 (unused helper at src/guard.mjs:20). N3 is Minor, so it becomes a nit.
    - Under deliver-nits, N3 is folded into delivery. No replyable comment row results.
    - The digest's comments are replaced only after this review completes.
    - Claims and dispositions carry forward. No claim re-check or whole-wave review runs.
12. **Exit check.** Readiness fails on N3, and usage is 1/10, so the loop continues.

## D3 iteration 2 (head 2222222)

1. **Setup.**
   - The boundary refresh is unchanged.
   - Record `pre_wave_head = 2222222` and `round_start_head = 2222222`.
   - `fetch origin main` and `merge-tree` both succeed, with `merge-tree` exiting 0.
2. **Implementer for N3.** I dispatch a fresh `implementer` with cwd `/work/widgets-pr-42` and the same rules, scoped test and scope baseline. It returns `done` with one commit and a clean tree. I persist `rounds_used 2`.
3. **Pre-push review.** A fresh `wave-reviewer` reviews `2222222..HEAD` with N3 carried and the fix delta `git diff 2222222 HEAD`. It returns `N3: resolved` with no new finding.
4. **Push.**
   - The done-check passes.
   - Compare-and-swap still shows 2222222, the body unchanged and `main`.
   - The same push command succeeds, and I persist `pushed_head` and `headRefOid = 3333333`.
5. **Watch.** CI succeeds on 3333333 with nothing pending, so the watch is skipped.
6. **Own-push re-render.**
   - Refresh with `gh pr view` and `gh run list -c 3333333...`.
   - Re-run the two comment fetches and the `reviewThreads` query.
   - The last re-review has no nit or blocker. `repair.wave` is cleared after reconciliation.
7. **Exit check: readiness.**
   - CI evidence is on 3333333 and every claim has a disposition.
   - The PR is MERGEABLE and CLEAN, with no failing or binding pending check.
   - There is no unreviewed comment delta.
   - The tree is tracked-clean and synced with the remote.
   - `gh api repos/acme/widgets --jq '{allow_squash_merge,allow_merge_commit,allow_rebase_merge}'` permits squash.
   - Every opted-in and later-minted nit has a resolved line, so readiness is met and the final menu renders.

## Assessed head

- Verification and the brief assess **3333333333333333333333333333333333333333**.
- The evidence source is CI on that exact head. No local verification command ran; helpers ran only the scoped tests.
- No `Sync:` line renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

## Report and menu

```text
Evidence: CI (source: ci) on 3333333 - ci / test success; 0 binding pending; merge_state_status CLEAN.
Delivers: the PR rejects unsigned events.
Role: author

Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (ci / test)

Not offered: approve (your own PR)

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge PR 42 at 3333333 with --match-head-commit. [recommended]
2. stop - leave the checkout and branch as they are and end the run.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI on 3333333: ci / test success, 0 binding pending, merge_state_status CLEAN).
```

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved on this case: both outputs dispatch N1 and N2 on the already-mergeable head instead of exiting readiness, both fold N3 from the own-push re-review into the next wave under deliver-nits with no fresh nit selection, and both render the final menu only after N1/N2/N3 are `resolved`, the assessed head is the exact pushed head 3333333 with CI success, and merge is still a separate numbered pick rather than an automatic action. The Change targets the batch summary round and no-arg discovery paths, which this single-argument case never reaches, so the per-PR sequencing wording is inert here; the only visible drift in After is cosmetic (`code-reviewer` renamed to `wave-reviewer`, an added `allow_squash_merge` read, `--match-head-commit` on the merge line), none of which touches the three facts. Keep the After wording as is for this path; just make sure the batch-summary sequencing text is scoped to the no-arg multi-PR round so it cannot leak into the single-PR D3 loop and introduce an extra menu between waves.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved on this case: both outputs dispatch separate implementers for N1 and N2 despite the head already being mergeable, both carry N3 straight into a second wave under the retained deliver-nits course without re-rendering a nit menu, and both reach the final report only after explicit reviewer closure lines for all three nits, exact-head refresh on 3333…, and successful CI, with merge left as a menu pick that is never executed. Two After-only drifts are worth tightening even though they did not flip a fact here: the final evidence line cites 'run 910' against head 3333…, but run 910 was the digest's run on the original head 1111… and the Entry never supplied a run id for the later heads, so the wording should either omit the run id or say 'exact-head run (id not supplied)' to avoid inventing a result beyond the snapshots; and the heading 'Final report and first menu' leaks the new batch-summary per-PR sequencing vocabulary into a single-PR run, which could confuse a reader into expecting more menus — scope the 'first PR / next PR' phrasing strictly to the batch summary round so single-argument runs keep the plain 'Final report and menu' header. Also keep the helper agent name consistent with Before ('code-reviewer' vs After's 'wave-reviewer') unless the rename is intentional.
